benchmarks: KernelEvolve (production accelerator-kernel optimizer, Meta, internal controlled study)
fallos_mitigaciones: Buggy nodes trigger expensive debug-retry loops; cross-session memory reuse cuts the buggy-node fraction from 55% to 34% (p=0.1) / 21% (p=0.5), driving the 52% token-cost saving (§6). But higher injection anchors the search (p=0.5 collapses to 8 strategy combinations vs 20 cold-start, and the single best solution comes from no-memory, 1.49x vs 1.36x) -- an open exploration-anchoring tradeoff (§7).
cita: Liao et al. (2026). Experience Graphs: The Data Foundation for Self-Improving Agents.
notes: mem_tipos: the paper unifies 3 existing knowledge tiers (declarative=SEMANTICA via CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md, procedural=PROCEDIMENTAL via skills, episodic=EPISODICA via session transcripts, §3) plus an orthogonal 4th tier, the 'experience graph' (causal tree of attempts with rewards, Table 1) which does not map 1:1 to the closed vocabulary; annotated as additional EPISODICA (records of past attempts with timestamps/lineage). representacion=GRAFO;VECTOR: 'tree/DAG: nodes with parent links, rewards, siblings' (Table 1) + task-description embeddings for cross-session vector similarity (§4, under a 4-table relational schema with Cypher over foreign keys). operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION: 'Writes are a mix of appends (new nodes) and localized path updates (MCTS backpropagation walks the ancestor chain to update visit counts and cumulative rewards)' (§3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: each outer-loop step persists its result after each inner-loop invocation (§2). retrieval=GRAFO;EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: 'Reuse: Find similar prior tasks via vector search, then retrieve their high-fitness subtrees via graph traversal' (Table 2) + frontier selection ordered by fitness/UCB. mide_lectura=SI: §6 measures the effect of injecting prior memory (cross-session reuse probability p) on convergence speed/cost/failures (Fig.3). alcance=PROYECTO;ORGANIZACION: 'Collectivity' is an explicit substrate requirement -- 'a proven playbook should be reusable organization-wide'; 'governed cloud store, cross-user, cross-session' (Table 1). multiagente=SI: contribution 1 explicitly extends to 'multi-agent scientific societies' + a dedicated 'Concurrent multi-agent search' subsection (atomic backprop across workers, §5). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'Time travel: CDC changelog -> AS-OF reconstruction at any step' + 'Audit: Trace which prior attempts...influenced a given decision' (Table 1/2); governance inherits access policy from source episodes (§3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;MULTIAGENTE (MULTIAGENTE added vs F_screening for the dedicated architectural treatment, though not empirically benchmarked in the KernelEvolve controlled study). handoff=PUNTEROS;CONTENIDO;CONTRATO: 'a child node either inherit its parent's session as a cheap resume [PUNTEROS via session_id/parent_id] or reconstruct context from the graph' [CONTENIDO]; Tasks define 'specification, target environment, and success metric' [CONTRATO] received by each session (§4). plan_estado=SI: 'Sessions record who is searching, with which algorithm, and how far they have gotten' (§4, search progress as memory content).

benchmarks: SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, SWE-Bench Pro
fallos_mitigaciones: Fixed compression rules cannot adapt to the heterogeneous value of information (code inspected early may remain essential later; verbose logs can be compressed anytime), Fig.1(a)(b); mitigated by proactive, flexible, agent-decided compression based on trajectory state (§1-2.1). Training-data quality filters guard against defects: inappropriate reduction ratio (>80% or <20%), overly short compression ranges, range misalignment (§2.2.2).
cita: Gao et al. (2026). SWE-MeM: Learning Adaptive Memory Management for Long-Horizon Coding Agents.
notes: mem_tipos=TRABAJO: manages the interaction-history/context of a single repair trajectory under a token budget (§2.1, Eq.1), not memory persisted across tasks. representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: memory entries {c}(summary) and {f}(remaining_work) are plain text inserted into the trajectory (Eq.2), no vector/graph. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION: the compress() tool replaces a raw span with a higher-level summary (§2.1, analogous to Semantic Consolidation). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;PRESUPUESTO: the agent proactively decides when/what/how to compress based on trajectory state (central contribution) + a probabilistic scheduler activated when context budget drops below 20%, reaching 1 at 5% remaining (§2.2.1). retrieval=NA: no external-store retrieval mechanism; compressed content stays inline in context. mide_lectura=NO (matches F_screening, no RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO). alcance=TAREA: memory management scoped to a single repository-repair task (SWE-Bench). fidelidad_procedencia=NO. benchmarks=SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, SWE-Bench Pro (§3.1, §4.3). metricas=EXITO(resolve rate, Table1/3)+COSTO-TOKENS(Token Usage, Table2)+ITERACION(Average Step, Table2). evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Fig.4: proactive-vs-threshold, selective-vs-full-summarization, curriculum SFT, memory-aware GRPO, memory-tool removal)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1/3)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table2: relative token/step usage). F=CONSOLIDACION;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). handoff=NO: intra-trajectory/intra-task memory management, does not cross sessions or agents (remaining_work propagates WITHIN the same trajectory, §2.1). plan_estado=SI: 'remaining_work f records the remaining subtasks and is appended to the end of the trajectory to maintain task continuity' (§2.1) -- exactly plan/progress state as memory content.

fallos_mitigaciones: Intra-source noise (long-tail relevance-score distribution) mitigated via a dynamic MAD-based threshold (Eq.1, §3.3.2). Cross-source conflicts/staleness (an outdated preference like 'likes coffee' vs. fresher evidence) mitigated by an arbitration score weighing relevance+temporal freshness+source confidence (Eq.2, Beijing-trip example, §3.3.2).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: the abstract layer agglomerates 'episodic memory (event chains), semantic memory (entity graphs), and emotional memory (user preferences)' (§3.1.2); 'emotional memory' (preferences) has no dedicated token in the closed vocabulary and is mapped to SEMANTICA (abstracted user facts) for lack of a better fit. representacion=HIBRIDA: 'SemanticMap and SemanticGraph, which natively fuses key-value, vector, and graph structures' (§3.2, Fig.2) -- unifies KV+vector+graph in one in-memory structure. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: memory-unit creation (CRUD API, §3.2); the abstract layer agglomerates basic memories via LLM (CONSOLIDACION, §3.1.2); state-update edges track preference evolution (e.g. 'Wangfujing Hotel' -> 'hutong homestay', ACTUALIZACION, §3.1.2). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: the abstract layer 'leverages an LLM to agglomerate compact abstract memories' (§3.1.2); the basic layer writes each dialogue turn (event). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: hybrid recall runs BM25+SPLADE+dense vector in parallel, fused via reciprocal rank fusion, subgraph expansion for multi-hop, cross-encoder rerank (§3.3.1). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): retrieval accuracy reported in Table3/4 (LoCoMo 92.21%, LongMemEval 88.40%). alcance=SESION: cross-session memory is explicitly central ('cross-session, multi-typed information', Abstract). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: conflict resolution weighs 'temporal freshness' and 'source confidence', discards 'stale or redundant alternatives' (Eq.2, §3.3.2); traceable links 'source_unit_uids...allows the system to verify abstract evidence' (§3.1.2). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;FIDELIDAD (FIDELIDAD added vs F_screening for the dedicated staleness/conflict-resolution design pillar, §3.3.2). benchmarks=LoCoMo, LongMemEval (§5.1, Table3/4). metricas=OTRA(accuracy Table3/4)+COSTO-TOKENS('Avg. Tok.' column, Table3/4)+LATENCIA(5.4x retrieval speedup, 4.8x insertion speedup at 10 QPS, §1/§5.3). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(Table3/4)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency and RAM/GPU utilization, §5.3-5.4) -- no explicit ablation section was found in the reviewed text. handoff=CONTENIDO: linked events/facts persist and are retrieved across sessions (Mike's Beijing-trip example linking sessions, §3.1.2). plan_estado=NO.

benchmarks: SWE-bench Lite (matched 50-task-per-condition comparison); a separate unnamed 5-task comparison
fallos_mitigaciones: The 'read-try-fail-reread' loop: a failed patch attempt triggers another whole-file read or broad search, spending tokens without necessarily finding the missing evidence (§1.1); mitigated by 'retrieve broadly, expose narrowly' plus two-phase synchronization that prevents stale reads after edits (§3.1, §3.3).
cita: Luk et al. (2026). ContextSniper: AntTrail's Token-Efficient Code Memory for Repository-Level Program Repair.
notes: mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA: local memory scoped to the current repair task ('task-time local code memory...built from the current repository snapshot, queried during the current repair run', §2.2), explicitly NOT cross-task memory ('leaving room for future integration with cross-task experience memory'). representacion=HIBRIDA: AGFS hierarchy L0(abstract text)/L1(structured metadata: paths, symbols, graph relations, BM25 docs)/L2(source chunks with embeddings) -- fuses DOCS-ARCHIVOS+GRAFO+VECTOR (§3.2, Fig.3). operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION: memory-node creation (WRITE); an 'intention-aware context gate' filters what enters the prompt (ADMISION, §3.5); two-phase memory-repository synchronization after each agent action keeps code memory aligned with edits (ACTUALIZACION, §3.3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: 'The first phase runs after agent actions through runtime hooks' (§3.3, each action triggers recording). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GREP-ARCHIVOS;GRAFO;RANKING: 'adaptive top-k retrieval that fuses semantic embeddings, BM25 lexical scoring, ctags-style symbolic metadata...and graph relations through weighted reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), with a ripgrep-based text-search fallback' (Contributions, §1.3). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): retrieved-evidence quality validated indirectly via resolution rates 'essentially unchanged' despite -51.5%/-38.9% tokens (Abstract, Fig.1C). alcance=TAREA: local memory for a single repair run, explicitly not cross-task. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'preserve provenance so the host agent can inspect and edit the source'; synchronization treats memory freshness as part of source grounding ('If retrieval returns an old version of a function after an edit, the compact context becomes actively harmful', §3.3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;FIDELIDAD (FIDELIDAD added vs F_screening for the dedicated synchronization/staleness mechanism, §3.3). metricas=COSTO-TOKENS(-51.5%/-38.9% total token use, -36.4%/-27.3% logged cost, Abstract)+EXITO(resolution rates 'essentially unchanged'). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(matched SWE-bench Lite comparison, Fig.1C)+MEDICION-COSTO(token/cost reduction) -- no explicit ablation section found. handoff=NO: local memory for a single task run, no explicit cross-session/cross-agent handoff protocol. plan_estado=NO.

fallos_mitigaciones: (1) Corpus content egress to a third-party model provider on every query = GDPR compliance risk, mitigated by the egress-bounded invariant (100% local retrieval, §3-4). (2) Aggressive key-sentence-extraction compression destroys 37.8% of tagged facts across the 41 test passages (41/41 lose >=1 fact), 'disqualifying' for enterprise use; mitigated by SEETR (only 1/41 passages loses a fact, §6.2). (3) Honest, unmitigated limitation: the paper's own retrieval-quality benchmark uses hash-based embeddings and therefore proves nothing about semantic-retrieval quality under the egress bound (§6.3, §7 item 1).
cita: Biancheri (2026). Egress-Bounded Retrieval: A Privacy-Preserving Enterprise Memory Architecture with No External Model in the Retrieval Path.
notes: mem_tipos=SEMANTICA: declarative enterprise knowledge -- organisation documents, people and decisions, organized via standard ontologies (Org/schema.org/ArchiMate, §4.1), no per-session episodic dialogue component. representacion=HIBRIDA: 'Text, vectors and the relationship graph share a single PostgreSQL instance' (Abstract, §4.2) -- fuses DOCS-ARCHIVOS+VECTOR+GRAFO. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: ingestion/chunking/embedding (WRITE, §4.2); self-tuning Tier1-3 detects 'near-duplicates...candidate cross-team links, likely mis-filings' and applies reversible 'merges, re-classification' (CONSOLIDACION, §4.4); trust score decays over time without deletion (soft ACTUALIZACION, §4.2: 'stale material recedes without being deleted'). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: ingestion triggered by file arrival; self-tuning Tier2 triggered by real usage patterns (§4.4). retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: 5 parallel strategies -- structured lookup, multilingual full-text, dense semantic, people-to-artifact graph traversal, thematic summaries -- merged and re-ranked by a local cross-encoder (§4.3). mide_lectura=SI (correction vs F_screening 'COSTO' alone; RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO added to F per rule 3): NDCG@10/Recall@5/Recall@10/MRR table in §6.3, though the paper itself honestly discloses the harness uses hash embeddings (not a real encoder) and therefore does NOT establish semantic-retrieval quality -- 'This benchmark does not evaluate semantic retrieval' (§6.3), it only verifies the fusion pipeline is wired correctly. alcance=ORGANIZACION: 'One customer, one tenant; every query scoped and access-controlled' (§4.1), multi-tenant enterprise-wide system with RBAC. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: explicit time-decaying trust score per content type (§4.2, §4.4); source attribution as a scoring criterion in the planned agentic-baseline comparison (§6.4). F=COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;FIDELIDAD (two additions vs F_screening='COSTO': RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO for §6.3, FIDELIDAD for trust-decay/provenance as a first-class design pillar). benchmarks=NINGUNO: no established academic benchmark used (BEIR is mentioned but dismissed as unsuitable, §2); the paper builds its own ad-hoc corpora (511 production documents; 41 passages/627 facts for SEETR §6.2; 54 documents/25 queries for the retrieval harness §6.3). metricas=LATENCIA(p50/p95/p99 tables §6.1, HNSW 430x faster than JSONB fallback at 10K)+COSTO-TOKENS(SEETR: 12.8% savings retaining 99.8% of facts vs. 39.6% savings destroying 37.8% of facts with key-sentence, §6.2)+OTRA(NDCG@10, Recall@5/10, MRR, §6.3). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(§6.3 retrieval harness, with explicit validity caveats)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency §6.1, compression/tokens §6.2) -- the paper itself states in Limitations that there is NO measured ablation ('Re-ranking is the quality bottleneck...This is an observation, not a measured ablation', §7 item 3). handoff=NO: enterprise memory for human users via an assistant, not context handoff between LLM-agent sessions/agents. plan_estado=NO.

fallos_mitigaciones: 'Memory Inflation' and 'Contextual Degradation' (older critical info pushed out of the context window, 'stateless'/incoherent behavior, contradicting prior decisions) and 'self-degradation' of the naive 'All-Add' strategy due to 'catastrophic interference' (§1.2, §2.3, Fig.2); mitigated by the 'Intelligent Decay' mechanism (utility-based selective pruning/consolidation) plus HITL user pin/forget intervention (§3.2-4).
cita: Xu (2025). Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: Appendix A reveals that the Figure 2 data (the 'All-Add' vs 'Hybrid System' comparison over 500 turns) is generated by a Python script with HAND-CODED exponential-decay/logistic-drift formulas, with ranges explicitly 'clamped...for realistic visualization' -- NOT derived from real LLM-agent executions. §5.1 itself admits 'Through simulated long-running task experiments' and 'We conducted a series of simulated experiments', without specifying which LLM (if any) actually produced Table 1. Given the appendix evidence, the paper's empirical rigor is doubtful (possibly post-hoc invented data to illustrate the narrative); values are extracted AS THE PAPER PRESENTS THEM but flagged for human review. mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: explicit 3-component architecture -- 'Working Memory (WM)' (TRABAJO), 'Episodic Memory (EM)' a vector-DB of timestamped MemoryEntry (EPISODICA), 'Semantic Memory (SM)' of distilled abstract concepts/summaries (SEMANTICA) (§3.1). representacion=VECTOR: Episodic Memory is concretely implemented as a vector database with dense embeddings (§3.1); Semantic Memory is described with hedged/non-committal language ('potentially implemented as a fact collection or knowledge graph') and is therefore not confidently labeled. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;OLVIDO: MemoryEntry creation (WRITE); Algorithm 1 'ConsolidateToSemanticMemory(Mi)' via LLM summary (CONSOLIDACION, §3.3); explicit 'EpisodicMemory.Delete(Mi)' for low-utility entries (OLVIDO, Algorithm 1). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: decay decision by utility-score threshold S(Mi) < theta_decay (Algorithm 1, §3.2.1-3.2.2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING: cosine similarity Ei between memory vector and current-task vector, selection by composite Utility Score (§3.2.1). mide_lectura=NO (matches F_screening, no RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; §5.2 promises 'retrieval latency' as a Memory Metric but Table 1 does not actually report it). alcance=TAREA: a single long-running task (a multi-week software-project plan, 500 turns, §5.1), no explicit cross-session framing. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: a dedicated 'Contradiction Rate' metric measures when the agent's output conflicts with previously stated facts/instructions (§5.2) -- consistency between recalled and previously stated content, central to the paper's title. F=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;COSTO;NEGATIVO (NEGATIVO added vs F_screening: the paper explicitly documents the 'self-degradation' failure of the naive 'All-Add' strategy as a central finding, Fig.2, §5.3 -- negative evidence about naive memory management, though the evidence's rigor is doubtful, see RECONSIDERAR). benchmarks=NINGUNO: a self-built simulated task, no standard academic benchmark (§5.1). metricas=EXITO(Task Completion Rate)+COSTO-TOKENS(Average Token Cost per turn)+LATENCIA(Average Latency per turn)+OTRA(Consistency Score, Contradiction Rate) -- Table 1. evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA: since Appendix A shows at least Figure 2 was generated with hardcoded formulas (not measured from a real system), and the text itself calls its experiments 'simulated', it does not meet the real ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E bar (gate rule 2: 'demos and examples = CUALITATIVA'); see RECONSIDERAR. handoff=NO: memory for a single continuous task/agent, no explicit handoff protocol between distinct sessions or agents. plan_estado=NO: MemoryEntry objects are atomic interactions (message/tool-call/observation), not a dedicated plan/progress object.
